content: The use of red raspberry (Rubus idaeus, Rubus strigosus) leaf is associated with specific dosing recommendations depending on the indication. For oral consumption, 5 grams of leaves can be steeped in 150 mL of water, or 4-8 mL of a 1:1 preparation in 25% alcohol can be taken three times daily. Alternatively, 2 grams of dried leaf can be infused in 240 mL of water. This herbal preparation has been traditionally used for a variety of conditions, including cardiovascular disorders, diarrhea, dysmenorrhea, gastrointestinal disorders, support during labor and delivery, menorrhagia, prevention of miscarriage, morning sickness, and topical treatment for inflammation of the mouth, throat, or skin. It has also been used for respiratory disorders. However, evidence suggests little benefit compared to placebo in some cases. No adverse effects have been reported with its use. However, it is contraindicated in individuals with hormone-sensitive conditions such as breast cancer, endometriosis, ovarian cancer, uterine cancer, or uterine fibroids. Regarding pregnancy, an Australian study has shown no adverse outcomes associated with the use of red raspberry leaf during pregnancy. It is classified as generally acceptable for use during pregnancy, with controlled studies in pregnant women showing no evidence of fetal risk. There is no available data on its use during lactation.
